newsitem.title: INDIA: India deficit may bear some oil debt-FinMin source.
newsitem.headline: India deficit may bear some oil debt-FinMin source.

text.p: Transferring to the fiscal deficit just over half of India's 190 billion rupee ($5.3 billion) debt to domestic oil companies is one option under consideration, a senior Finance Ministry said on Monday.
"To my knowledge there are no specific proposals, but various ideas are being floated," he told Reuters.
But one idea in play was to consolidate up to 100 billion rupees of the oil pool deficit in the fiscal deficit over a period of one or two years.
"There is no intention of bearing the whole," he said.
He said the coalition was considering ways to increase petroleum product prices to neutralise the incremental increase in the oil pool deficit since the start of the fiscal year on April 1.

The oil pool deficit, which tallies money owed to oil companies for selling their products below market prices to support India's subsidy system, stood at 155 billion rupees at the end of 1996/97 on March 31.
The deficit ballooned late last year when India failed to raise domestic prices when world oil prices shot higher.
"Obviously the main thing we are looking at is the outstanding debt (built up before April 1)," he said.
The United Front coalition government's policy-making steering committee has failed in its last two meetings to solve the oil riddle, and a third meeting has been deferred several times already.

Sources in New Delhi said the government could announce measures in August, but the timing remained unclear as Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition is wrought with internal divisions that could divert its energies.

But the oil companies need money back fast to pay for crude oil supplies needed to keep their refineries working. They are already heavily indebted and are keeping supplies flowing on a hand-to-mouth basis, and lack funds for vital capital investment.

There has been some discussion that the government could provide some support for the oil pool deficit's past accumulations, and up to 100 billion rupees of the debt could be liquidated over one or two years, he said.
Other measures being talked about included reductions in customs duties on oil, but this would have an impact of government revenues, he added.
Press Trust of India reported earlier on Monday that the Finance Ministry was lowering its resistance to the idea of taking some of the oil pool deficit on its own account.
Ministry sources said the fiscal deficit is unlikely to rise above 5.2 percent of gross domestic product if the oil pool deficit was added to the government's books, the news agency reported.
The agency quoted Finance Ministry sources as saying this figure was within manageable limits, although the 1997/98 budget targeted a deficit of 4.5 percent of GDP.

Consolidating the oil pool deficit in the government's overall debt, and paying for it by issuing "petro-bonds" was one proposal by a committee charged seeking ways to restructure the oil sector's finances. The Finance Ministry had originally opposed this idea, PTI said. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
